title: automate KMS/HSM/TLS rotation for private-installer, helm and terraform
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Automates rotation of TLS certificates and KMS/HSM keys for Private installer deployments. Adds a configurable rotation controller, Terraform inputs for KMS/ HSM keys, Helm templating for sealed-secrets and Vault integration, and upgrade/rollback safeguards.
description:
Context: Private deployments currently require manual orchestration to rotate TLS certs, KMS keys, and HSM-backed keys. Customers on long-lived air-gapped installs and managed VPCs requested an automated, auditable rotation flow that works with Vault, sealed-secrets (SOPS) and optional HSM-backed KMS. This PR implements an end-to-end automation path across the private-installer, Helm charts, and Terraform modules so rotations can be scheduled, audited, and rolled back.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a rotation controller to the private-installer (k8s controller + CronJob) that can rotate TLS certs for ingress, service mesh, and API endpoints with safe cutover. 2) Introduces a new terraform module (terraform/modules/kms-rotation) to manage KMS key versions and HSM wrapping keys with providers for AWS KMS, Google KMS, and an abstract interface for on-prem HSM (PKCS#11). 3) Helm chart updates: templates for sealed-secrets key injection, optional Vault sidecar injector, rolling update hooks, and templated certificates that support canary flips. 4) Operator tooling: a CLI (private-installer/scripts/rotate-kms-certs.sh) and an API endpoint for manual trigger + dry-run mode. 5) Upgrade/rollback: preflight checks and automatic rollback if post-rotation healthchecks fail. 6) Audit and observability: rotation events are emitted as structured audit logs, expose metrics (rotation_success, rotation_duration_seconds, rotation_failures) to the Redwood Console.

Integration tests include a local controller test harness and a terraform plan check (uses mocked providers in CI). Final CI summary: build: pass, unit tests: pass, integration: pass (controller harness), terraform-plan: pass, helm-lint: pass.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun: "Can you add a safety timeout for the canary window and make the rollback path explicit? We should also emit the previous cert version in the audit event."
  - Maya: "Added canaryWindowSeconds with default 300s and explicit rollback step in controller. Audit event now includes previousKeyVersion and previousCertFingerprint."
- Liam: "We need to ensure HSM PKCS#11 module path and slot config are optional and not logged. Also add a clear migration path for customers that used manual secret rotation scripts."
  - Maya: "HSM config moved to a sealed secret; controller only reads from in-cluster KMS config. Added migration doc with step-by-step and a CLI helper to import existing keys into the rotation state machine."
- Sofia: "Integration test seems flaky in CI due to timing; can we make healthchecks poll with exponential backoff?"
  - Maya: "Switched to exponential backoff and increased integration harness timeouts. Added additional assertions to avoid racey state checks."
- Priya: "Security review: confirm that wrapped keys are never persisted in logs and that Vault tokens are short-lived with renewal."
  - Maya: "Confirmed and added e2e secret scrubber. Vault token lifetimes are configurable and defaults are secure. Added docs section on KMS/HSM secrets handling."

Upgrade notes: This is a backwards-compatible feature when rotation.enabled=false. Enabling rotation requires: 1) a migration run (private-installer migrate-rotation-state) if the cluster has existing manual secrets, 2) a sealed-secrets key to be present (or Vault configured), and 3) terraform updates to pass kms-rotation inputs. The default behavior is dry-run until admin flips rotation.enabled=true. The operator supports canary-first rollouts so operators can validate before global cut-over.

Rollback story: Controller keeps the previous cert and key version in a protected namespace and will re-seed the previous secret on healthcheck failures. The terraform module includes an output with the lastAppliedKeyVersion to aid script-assisted rollback.

Security considerations: HSM credentials and KMS master keys are not committed to git. Any HSM connector settings are stored in sealed-secrets or external Vault with ACLs. Controller logs redact PKCS#11 module paths and key material. Audit events include key versions but not raw keys.

Docs: Updated docs/private-deployments/rotation.md with configuration examples for AWS KMS, Google KMS and a sample PKCS#11 HSM configuration. Added a troubleshooting section and recommended SRE alert rules for rotation_failures > 0.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals. Merge method: squash.

Notes for operators: Start in dry-run mode, run the provided migration helper, validate canary behavior in staging, then enable rotation for production. See docs/private-deployments/rotation.md for command examples and Terraform variables.
